description: Reading and writing external data in hundreds of formats, semantic import of tabular files, string- and byte-level conversion, and the specific format specifications most used for data, images, audio, documents and 3D geometry.

tools.name: Import
tools.description: Reads a file, URL or cloud object and converts it into a Wolfram Language expression, choosing the format from the extension or content. A second argument names the format, and a third selects an element such as "Data", "Elements" or a sheet name. It supports hundreds of formats including tabular, image, audio, geometry and scientific data.

parameters.name: "HeaderLines"
parameters.description: Number of header lines in tabular formats.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Directories to search for the file.

tools.notes: Import[file, "Elements"] lists what a given file can yield, which is the fastest way to explore an unfamiliar format.

tools.name: Export
tools.description: Writes an expression to a file in a specified or inferred format. Format-specific options control resolution, compression, encoding and metadata. It handles graphics, images, audio, video, data tables, notebooks and 3D geometry.
tools.usage:
Export["file", expr]
Export["file", expr, "format"]
Export["file", expr, opts]
tools.notes: Export returns the filename on success; use ExportString to get a string instead of writing a file.

tools.name: SemanticImport
tools.description: Imports tabular data while automatically interpreting each column semantically, producing dates, quantities, cities, currencies and other typed values in a Dataset. It removes most manual parsing work. Column interpreters can be specified explicitly when the automatic guess is wrong.
tools.notes: SemanticImportString does the same for data already held in a string.

tools.name: ImportString
tools.description: Parses a string as if it were the contents of a file in a given format. It avoids writing temporary files when data arrives from a web request or is embedded in code. All Import elements and options apply.

tools.name: ExportString
tools.description: Converts an expression into a string in a given format instead of writing it to a file. It is the natural counterpart of ImportString for in-memory pipelines and web responses. Binary formats produce byte-encoded strings.

tools.name: ImportByteArray
tools.description: Imports data directly from a ByteArray, which is the right tool for binary payloads received over the network or read from a socket. It accepts the same formats and elements as Import. Use it to avoid temporary files for binary data.

tools.name: ExportByteArray
tools.description: Serializes an expression into a ByteArray in a specified format. It is the binary counterpart of ExportString and is preferred for images, audio and archives. Use it when sending data through HTTP requests.

tools.name: CSV
tools.description: Comma-separated values, the most common plain-text tabular exchange format. Import returns a list of rows by default and can return a Dataset with the "Dataset" element. Options control header lines, delimiters and numeric interpretation.
tools.notes: TSV is the tab-separated equivalent; use "Table" for whitespace-delimited numeric files.

tools.name: TSV
tools.description: Tab-separated values, a tabular text format that avoids the quoting problems of commas in data. It shares all elements and options with CSV. Use it when fields may contain commas.

tools.name: XLSX
tools.description: Microsoft Excel workbook format. Import returns a list of sheets, each a list of rows, and elements such as "Sheets" or "Data" select parts. Export writes one or several named sheets from an association.

tools.name: JSON
tools.description: JavaScript Object Notation, the standard format for web APIs and configuration. The "JSON" format returns nested rules, while "RawJSON" returns associations and lists, which is usually more convenient. Export serializes associations, lists and strings.
tools.notes: Prefer "RawJSON" for programmatic use; "JSON" gives rule-based output kept for compatibility.

tools.name: XML
tools.description: Extensible Markup Language, imported as a symbolic XMLObject tree that can be queried with pattern matching. Elements such as "XMLElement" and "Plaintext" give different views. Use it for structured documents, SVG and many scientific formats.
tools.example: xml = ImportString["12", "XML"]; Cases[xml, XMLElement["b", _, {v_}] :> v, Infinity]

tools.name: HDF5
tools.description: Hierarchical Data Format version 5, widely used for large scientific arrays with metadata. Elements such as "Datasets", "DataFormat" and explicit dataset paths select parts of the file. Use it for multi-gigabyte numeric data with named groups.

tools.name: MAT
tools.description: MATLAB workspace format, imported as named arrays and structures. Elements such as "LabeledData" return an association of variable names to values. Use it to exchange numeric data with MATLAB workflows.

tools.name: WAV
tools.description: Uncompressed PCM audio format. Import returns an Audio object by default, or raw sample data with the "AudioData" element. Export writes Audio and Sound objects with a chosen bit depth and sample rate.

tools.name: PNG
tools.description: Lossless raster image format with alpha channel support. Import returns an Image, and Export accepts images, graphics and any rasterizable expression. ImageResolution and "ColorSpace" options control output quality.
tools.example:
Export["fig.png", Plot3D[Sin[x y], {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2}],
  ImageResolution -> 200, Background -> None]
tools.notes: Use JPEG for photographs where file size matters, TIFF for high-bit-depth scientific images.

tools.name: PDF
tools.description: Portable Document Format, supported for both vector export of graphics and import of pages, text and images. Elements such as "Plaintext", "Pages" and "Images" extract different content. Use it for publication-quality figures and document processing.

tools.name: SVG
tools.description: Scalable Vector Graphics, an XML-based vector format ideal for web publication. Export preserves curves and text as vectors rather than pixels. Import converts the drawing into Wolfram Language graphics primitives.

tools.name: STL
tools.description: Stereolithography format storing a triangulated surface, the standard interchange for 3D printing. Import returns Graphics3D or a MeshRegion with the "MeshRegion" element. Export accepts Graphics3D, meshes and regions.
tools.notes: STL carries no units or color; Printout3D handles printing-service submission.

tools.name: OBJ
tools.description: Wavefront OBJ format for 3D geometry, supporting vertices, normals, texture coordinates and material references. It is more expressive than STL and widely supported by 3D tools. Import returns Graphics3D or mesh elements.
tools.notes: PLY and DXF are the other commonly used 3D interchange formats supported by Import and Export.

tools.name: Table
tools.description: Whitespace-delimited plain-text tabular format, the natural choice for columns of numbers written by scientific programs. Import returns a list of rows with numbers already parsed. Field separators and header handling are configurable.

tools.name: Text
tools.description: Plain text format, imported as a single string or as lines with the "Lines" element. It is the simplest way to read logs, source files and unstructured content. Character encoding is controlled with the CharacterEncoding option.

tools.name: GeoJSON
tools.description: JSON-based format for geographic features, imported as GeoPosition-based geometry and properties. It is the standard exchange format for web mapping. Use it to bring boundaries and point layers into GeoGraphics.

tools.name: Parquet
tools.description: Columnar binary format used widely in data engineering, offering efficient compressed storage of large tables. Import can return a Dataset directly and supports column selection. Use it for large analytical datasets.

tools.name: ZIP
tools.description: Compressed archive format. Import lists the contained file names or extracts specific entries, and Export creates archives from files or expressions. Use it to bundle results and to read data without unpacking to disk.
tools.notes: ExtractArchive and CreateArchive give a more explicit file-oriented interface.

tools.name: FileFormat
tools.description: Determines the format of a file from its content and extension, returning the format name Import would use. It is useful when processing directories of mixed files. Pair it with Import to dispatch on type.

tools.name: FileNames
tools.description: Lists files matching a string pattern in one or more directories, optionally recursing to a given depth. It is the standard way to enumerate inputs for batch processing. Patterns use the usual string wildcards.

tools.name: FileSystemMap
tools.description: Applies a function to every file under a directory tree, optionally filtered by a pattern and limited in depth. It returns a nested association mirroring the directory structure. Use it for batch import, conversion or analysis.
